newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's oil investors plan talks with PDVSA.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's oil investors plan talks with PDVSA.

text.p: Foreign investors in Venezuela's oil sector are expected to hold meetings with state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) for four days from Tuesday to clarify technical and legal issues surrounding the forthcoming third round of operating licences, foreign investors said Monday.

High on the agenda will be municipal taxes -- taxes levied by local councils -- which are not covered by current operating contracts, but can seriously diminish the profitability of the licences, potential investors say.

"There are some issues which have not been totally resolved like the issue of municipality taxes; these burdens can become very large and should be clarified from the beginning," said Horacio Begaries, managing director of Perez Companc Venezuela.

In an interview with Reuters, he said municipality taxes in one region where his company was working rose threefold without any warning. The discretionary rates are set at irregular intervals by local legislators anywhere between two and seven percent of gross revenues, and investors say they should be standardised by law.
Other items on the table include new methods of cost accounting proposed in the third round contracts.
The contracts specify that PDVSA subsidiaries reimburse operating costs and capital expenditure to the operator and also pay a per-barrel fee which is negotiated between the two parties.
Some investors believe that the money should go to regional state funds instead of local governments to minimise the risk of corruption.
The meetings between PDVSA and investors will take place in Macuto, on the north Venezuelan coast.
The third round of operating licences is due to be awarded in May, but PDVSA has not announced an exact date, nor the order in which the 20 "marginal" fields will be awarded.
Foreign investors say the order in which the contracts are announced will influence their bidding strategy.
